properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2021 to BEECH RESOURCES LLC in Lycoming Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEECH RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 914301
Permit API: 081-21812
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/19/2021
Comments: On April 19, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an investigation of a reported spill (CTS No. 356072) at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported on April 19, 2021, after removing the second AST off the well pad an area of high conductivity and staining was observed in the highly compacted soil where the tank was located. The estimated volume of the spill was about 500 gallons of production fluid. The area of impact was about 120 ft. X 150 ft. circle with varying levels of conductivity. A contractor was onsite beginning to excavate the impacted soils. The contractor was removing about 6 to 8 inches of impacted soil. The area of impact was screened by Beech Resources for conductivity. Areas where the compacted soil had already been removed had a conductivity near 320 uS/cm to 910 uS/cm. Conductivity of areas that had not yet been excavated at the time were around 1.69 mS/cm. There were no seeps off the well pad observed. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect confirmatory samples on April 20, 2021. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection Reports 3139277 and 3141035 still remain.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/02/2022 to DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in New Vernon Twp, Mercer county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/02/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 954014
Permit API: 085-22185
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: New Vernon Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/02/2022
Comments: Responded to an oil spill at this gas well location. The plug for the heater tube in the stock tank failed and allowed oil to leak out of the tank and into the diking. With the recent heavy rains, it appears the fluid in the diking overflowed through an open freshwater drain pipe and an inadequate diking height in spots. There was a ditch located on the backside of the diking where some of the oil flowed into but most of the oil appears to have gone out the freshwater drain pipe and then down the lease road. The lease road was approximately 55 yards long and pockets of oil were located throughout it and then into the weeds heading towards that same ditch that runs parallel to the lease road. The ditch empties into the Lake Wilhelm Road ditch. This Lake Wilhelm Road ditch just had a sheen of oil of oil on it west of the driveway. The last spot oil was seen in this ditch was about 10 yards east of the driveway culvert pipe outfall. No oil or sheen was seen emptying into or in the main stream of Calvin Clark Run itself. The oil was mostly contained with sorbent pads and by the grass and brush in the ditch. Based on site observations, it appears that less than 1 bbl of oil was released outside the diking area. With the heavy rains predicted again in the next 2 days, it was suggested for them to install a siphon dam in the field ditch right before it enters into the road ditch. A small excavator arrived on site and was in the process of doing this when I left. They were getting a vac truck out there today to remove all the fluid in the tank to stop the leaking of the oil. At 3:31 PM, Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy called me. He reported that they had just removed around 50 bbls of old motor oil from that stock tank. He said this well produces very little fluid and it was definitely old oil (he thinks motor oil). So he feels somebody had apparently dumped old motor oil in this tank. He said that he is probably going to file a police report on this incident.

Comments: This inspection is in response to a complaint of a spill on 03/07/2022 located at the Armac lease on Bauer Hill road. The complainant reported a strong smell and saw diapers and oil booms in the Bauer Hill road ditch as well as inside the containment diking. Upon responding to the complaint, and speaking with Vince Bailey the pumper for the lease he reported that the storage tank had over flowed on Saturday March 5th, he cleaned up the oil inside containment he estimated the spill at 2.5 barrels. Monday crude oil had breached the diking by migrating through the pervious material used in the construction of the containment. The crude oil flowed down slope approx 250 feet into a road side ditch on Bauer Hill road, it continued another 275 feet into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Glade Run. There was evidence of crude along the tributary to its confluence of Glad Run. An unknown amount of crude oil was released and made its way into waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On April 19, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report that was received by the Department on April 18, 2024 at 7:50 PM. The report states the spill, that reportedly occurred on April 18, 2024 at approximately 6:10 PM, was approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid. Act 9 sign is present on site (Photo 1). PPC and ERP plans are both present on site (Photos 2-3).The Department was met on site by Derek Zofchak and Nick Reda of Range Resources, along with other crew who were working on the hydraulic line repair of the bulldozer on site. According to the operator, approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released to the ground from a bulldozer during construction activities. The bulldozer unexpectedly stopped as it was tracking over a newly graded area of the site when the crew observed the hydraulic fluid on the ground where the dozer had been traveling. Range Resources then scraped approximately 2-3 inches of the newly graded and now impacted soil and placed it into two roll off boxes, which have been since removed from the site to be disposed. The area of impact can be seen in Photos 4-7 where the soil is no longer tracked on top. According to Range Resources, the bulldozer remains at the location where it shut down, as pictured, while a crew is actively working to repair the line. Violations are being noted and immediately corrected. The Department requests disposal documents when they are made available to the Operator.

Comments: On March 4, 2020, the Operator reported the following: “The incident occurred at the Moritz Well Pad. Reportedly, 126 gallons of produced water was released while GPUs were being blown down. A 1/2 valve was left open and the produced water back fed into the GPU line and was released to the GPU skid and gravel pad. All produced water was reportedly removed. Range is prepared to rig down GPU's for remediation. A vac truck is on standby in case heavy precipitation event occurs overnight. Crews will be on scene tomorrow. No waterways reportedly impacted.” On March 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection to a release of fluid to the well pad reported on 3/4/2020. I was accompanied by Range representative Brandon Carson. According to Mr. Carson a needle valve on the 3H GPU was left open after it was blown down for snubbing operation, snubbing is act of adding a smaller diameter tubing to a well to increase the flow rate of the well. The release occurred when the common dump line flowed back into the 3H GPU, overflowing the 3H GPU and causing fluid to be lost to the well pad surface via an open needle valve on the 3H GPU. The GPUs were not placed in secondary containment at the time of the release. During the inspection, the Operator was working to disconnect the 3H GPU to move the unit and remediate the impacted location. No waterways were impacted by the release. The Operator is incompliance with the current spill policy and intends to utilize Act 2 for remediation of a release greater than 42 gallons. Violations are being issued for the release of a regulated fluid to the ground. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 348342

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/09/2021 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Twp, Tioga county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/09/2021
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 910055
Permit API: 117-20562
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/09/2021
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the Seneca Resources - Gee 832 Well Site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/9/21 @0950 hours. The weather was 45 degrees and sunny. No activity or personnel was observed onsite. The site consists of a long access road, well pad and perimeter controls. The majority of the well pad was clear of snow and ice with some piles still melting along the edges. Frozen fluid was observed in the infiltration basin off the corner of the well pad. What appeared to be frost was observed on the production tank onsite. Upon closer inspection, the tank appeared to be covered in crystalized salt originating from the top hatch of the tank . The front 1/3 of the "Highland" production tank and a small ~5'x5' area in front of the tank were observed to have the salt material on it. The pad surface in front of the tank was observed damp. Soil conductivity of the damp area was measured with a Groline soil conductivity probe and found to be >4.0mS/cm directly adjacent to the yellow barrel. Other areas screened within the 5'x5' area in front of the tank were found to have a field measured conductivity of 2.18mS/cm and 1.7mS/cm. Due to the lack of cell phone service onsite, I traveled to a nearby well pad with known cell phone service to contact the operator. I then returned to the well site to complete the inspection. Seneca representative Jake Chambers arrived onsite in response to the release. Mr. Chambers and I discussed the possible causes for the release and the impacted area. Mr. Chambers stated he would immediately mobilize people and equipment to wash down the tank and remove any impacted pad material Jeff Passerrello, Seneca Resources, submitted confirmation of the remediation of the release at the Gee 832 Well Pad via email. Mr. Passerrello stated the release was estimated to have happened between Sunday 3/7/21 and the morning of the DEP inspection. The operator had unloaded the wells to the production tanks on Sunday, which they believe caused a mist of production fluid to coat the tank and gravel. The release was estimated to be approximately 5 gallons. Crews removed the impacted gravel, which was placed into 3 drums. A depth of 3" of material was removed from in front of the tank. The tank was also cleaned with freshwater and scrub brushes. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately Corrected: 25 Pa Code 78a57(a)Control, Storage and disposal of production fluids CSL402(b)Potential Pollution SWMA 301 Management of residual waste I departed the site at 1145 hours.

Comments: On March 27, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Shotski 7H well in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 3/25/2023. The report indicted that approximately 5-10 gallons of production fluid was released from a washed out pipe within GPU 7.The Act 9 site ID, PPC plan and ER plan were on site.At the time of inspection the Operator was decommissioning the GPUs. According to the on site representative the GPUs will be removed from the location and replaced.I observed staining and excavation around the 7H GPU. I utilized a conductivity probe to collect readings within the impacted area (photos 7,8 and 9).The impacted area appeared to be approximately 20' wide and 40' long and 2 to 12 inched in depth. The 7H GPU did not appear to be contained within secondary containment. The Shotski wells are not included within the 12/17/2020 Secondary Containment COA. I also collected a conductivity reading within the 7H self contained GPU (photo 13).The release appears to be contained to the well pad surface. Violation are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid and failure to design and construct the well site with secondary containment.

Inspection Date: 9/28/2023
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (7) wells on the Susan pad. The Susan 2H, 4H and the 5H are older wells and the 24HC, 25HC, 125HC and the 126HC were recently completed. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Susan 4H and 5H completed on 5/26/2021. This is the fifth testing since initial remedial work was performed. SPBUTs were initiated on 9/25/23 @ ~10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (7) wells annuli are shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Giordani Dicupillo and Creston Consultant Reps. Dakota Manning and Tiffany Smith. Starting at approx. 10:00am, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Rep., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. - See pic #1 for the pressures and flows at the start of the SPBUTs on 9/25/23). - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the Susan wells: - Susan 2H (20x13): Open top conductor (13x9): 0.0 psi..; 96% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:30 ** (9x5): 8 psi.; 100% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:34 - Susan 4H (20x13): Open top conductor (13x9): 169 psi.; 73% CH4; Sample collected @ 12:02 (9x5): 150 psi.; 78% CH4; Sample collected @ 12:04 - Susan 5H (20x13): 18 psi.; 70% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:40 (13x9): 4 psi.; 43% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:46 (9x5): 223 psi.; 58% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:50 - Susan 24HC (20x13): 0 psi.; 2,380ppm and dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 4 psi.; 95% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:30 ** (9x5): 3.1 psi.; 100% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:35 - Susan 25HC (20x13): 0 psi.; 600 ppm and dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 0 psi.; 66% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:44 ** (9x5): 181 psi.; 66% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:50 - Susan 125HC (20x13): 0 psi.; 20% and dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 3 psi.; 99% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:02 (9x5): 37 psi.; 64% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:06 - Susan 126HC (20x13): 0 psi.; 35% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:15 (13x9): 2 psi.; 100% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:18 ** (9x5):2 psi.; 100% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:22 (**) - Although no flows were noted at surface, The Dept. requests that Operator supply a report assessing the isotopic analysis of the annular gas samples collected and a plan to further evaluate and address the source of gas detected in these cemented (13x9) annuli, within 30 days. The plan should also include a schedule for heightened annular monitoring of these wells and a mechanical integrity assessment performed by a licensed engineer. The Dept. also requests that all these wells annuli remain open and venting in a safe manner, except for annual mechanical integrity testing as required in 78a.88. - Slight bubbling was noted in the cellar of the Susan 4H well. The lease operator contacted the Production dept. and the bubbling will be further investigated and corrective action will be taken. The Operator will inform the Department when work is complete and a follow up inspection (FUI) will be scheduled. - All (7) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank and the (20x13) annuli were opened to vent via Sentry valves @ 12:17

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/22/2025
Comments: On July 22, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3985188 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3985188, remedial excavation was completed and the impacted soil was stockpiled onsite awaiting disposal. The impacted soil stockpiles were covered and appeared to be adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 2). However, leaking gas was audible from the top of the well head (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The brine tank that was present at the time of the Department's previous surface inspection has been replaced. The newly-installed brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no elevated soil conductivity detected underneath the brine tank valve (see photos 7-9 and 18). It appears that the stained material noted underneath the brine tank during the time of IR 3967072 has been removed (see photo 10). It appears that the impacted soil stockpiles have been removed from site, as they were not present onsite during this inspection.The slope that was impacted by the 4/24/2025 release has been backfilled, mulched, and seeded. It has established some vegetative coverage, although it is inconsistent at the time of inspection (see photos 11, 13, and 14). An erosion rill has developed at the top of this slope (see photo 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) and straw bales are installed at the bottom of the formerly impacted slope (see photo 15). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this location or at the approximate downslope edge of the formerly impacted area (see photos 16-18).The Department notified the operator of the erosion rill observed during this inspection via voicemail, and recommended that it is repaired and measures are taken to protect it from heavy stormwater events while it establishes vegetative coverage.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remedial work has been completed and the site awaits completion of re-stabilization. However, violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding, as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.Additional violations may be forthcoming pending reassessment and reevaluation of the erosion rill in a future follow-up inspection conducted by the Department.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8235147
Permit API: 015-23438
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-04-29
Comments: Today's inspection was conducted in response to SWN self-reporting of a spill identified initially by DTE and then reported to SWN. The spill occurred on the ROW of the DTE Susquehanna Gathering Well Connect 67 Pipeline at a waterline valve cellar located at latitude 41.876168 and longitude -75.583155 also located in Jackson Township. The waterline was installed by DTE but is owned and operated by SWN. On 4/25/19, DTE operations personnel were conducting an annual inspection of their Well Connect 67 Pipeline and identified a three quarter inch line with a leaking quarter turn ball relief valve located above the lid of the waterline valve cellar, as shown in Photo #1. Photo #2 shows the extent of the accelerated corrosion caused by the leak to the lid. The DTE Operations personnel then contacted their Operations management team who then contacted SWN's Production group at 1:30 PM, that same day, 4/25/19. On 4/26/19 at 1:40 PM, SWN confirmed that the water within the cellar did show elevated conductivity. On 4/26/19 at 3:01 PM, Mike Deming, SWN Senior Regulatory Analyst left a voice message on my cell phone. Mr. Deming then attempted to contact Briana Cunningham at 3:01 PM and left a voice message. At 3:05 PM, Briana Cunningham contacted Mike Deming by phone who then explained the conditions listed above and noted that their conductivity readings showed the conductivity of the water within the valve cellar to be above the meter's capability of 19.9 milli Siemens. SWN measured the soil conductivity just off the valve cellar lid where the leak was running off the lid to be at 6.27 milli Siemens.
